✳ nightwatch.

Made for the moments between sunset and sunrise.

Weather: Open-Meteo · Astronomy: SunCalc · Seeing/transparency: ECCC/CMC

Forecast data and missing values

Weather forecasts come from Open-Meteo: cloud cover, relative humidity, temperature, dew point, wind speed, and precipitation probability. Forecasts are model outputs, not measurements at your telescope.

Seeing and transparency are provider-issued CMC/ECCC RDPS indices from MSC GeoMet, loaded for the selected location and exact UTC forecast hour. They are not arcseconds or measurements at your telescope. The model grid is about 10 km and covers North America. Provider condition labels, valid time, and model run are displayed. No temporal interpolation, extrapolation, or derived conversion is used. Missing or invalid values remain null. A combined viewing score is not supplied and remains null. Missing weather values also remain null, with no interpolation or substitution.

Sun and Moon geometry and illumination are calculated with SunCalc. Darkness means the Sun is below −18°. Twilight crossings are calculated to one-minute resolution, not supplied as measured data.

Dew guidance is a rule, not a dew prediction: use a heater when relative humidity is at least 85% or the air/dew-point spread is at most 3°C (5.4°F). Otherwise a heater is not indicated by those thresholds; keep it available. Missing any required input makes the recommendation null. No optical surface temperature is available.

The 24/48/72-hour tabs start now. Each row represents the upcoming hourly forecast timestamp, displayed in the location’s time zone. Links to observing guides do not imply a verified event or visibility forecast.
